answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by pricing identity through a bonded reputation prism: each agent locks a stake that vests slowly, like sand piling into a dune, cheap to start yet costly to fake at scale. New agents begin on a low-trust mesa with tiny transaction limits and must earn attestations from established peers before limits rise. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes and waiting out a thousand vesting periods, while one honest agent pays that cost once. Attack cost scales with every fake identity; verification cost stays flat.
